verses.zh: 祸哉！以法莲的酒徒，住在肥美谷的山上，他们心里高傲，以所夸的为冠冕，犹如将残之花。
verses.en: The splendid crown of Ephraim’s drunkards is doomed,[NOTE:1] the withering flower, its beautiful splendor,[NOTE:2] situated[NOTE:3] at the head of a rich valley,the crown of those overcome with wine.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Woe [to] the crown [or “wreath”] of the splendor [or “pride”] of the drunkards of Ephraim.” The “crown” is Samaria, the capital city of the northern kingdom (Ephraim). Priests and prophets are included among these drunkards in v. 7.
Heb “the beauty of his splendor.” In the translation the masculine pronoun (“his”) has been replaced by “its” because the referent (the “crown”) is the city of Samaria.
Heb “which [is].”

Heb “ones overcome with wine.” The words “the crown of” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The syntactical relationship of the final phrase to what precedes is uncertain. הֲלוּמֵי יָיִן (halume yayin, “ones overcome with wine”) seems to correspond to שִׁכֹּרֵי אֶפְרַיִם (shikkore ʾefrayim, “drunkards of Ephraim”) in line 1. The translation assumes that the phrase “the splendid crown” is to be understood in the final line as well.

verses.zh: 看哪，主有一大能大力者，像一阵冰雹，像毁灭的暴风，像涨溢的大水，他必用手将冠冕摔落于地。
verses.en: Look, the Lord[NOTE:1] sends a strong, powerful one.[NOTE:2] With the force of a hailstorm or a destructive windstorm,[NOTE:3] with the might of a driving, torrential rainstorm,[NOTE:4] he will knock that crown[NOTE:5] to the ground with his hand.[NOTE:6]
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here and in vv. 16, 22 is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “Look, a strong and powerful [one] belongs to the Lord.”
Heb “like a rainstorm of hail, a wind of destruction.”
Heb “like a rainstorm of mighty, overflowing waters.”
The words “that crown” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The object of the verb is unexpressed in the Hebrew text.
Or “by [his] power.”

verses.zh: 以法莲高傲的酒徒，他的冠冕必被踏在脚下。
verses.en: The splendid crown of Ephraim’s drunkardswill be trampled underfoot.

verses.zh: 那荣美将残之花，就是在肥美谷山上的，必像夏令以前初熟的无花果；看见这果的就注意，一到手中就吞吃了。
verses.en: The withering flower, its beautiful splendor,situated at the head of a rich valley, will be like an early fig before harvest—as soon as someone notices it,he grabs it and swallows it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “which the one seeing sees, while still it is in his hand he swallows it.”

verses.zh: 到那日，万军之耶和华必作他余剩之民的荣冠华冕，
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] the Lord of Heaven’s Armies will become a beautiful crown and a splendid diadem for the remnant of his people.
notes: Or “in that day” (KJV).

verses.zh: 也作了在位上行审判者公平之灵，并城门口打退仇敌者的力量。
verses.en: He will give discernment to the one who makes judicial decisionsand strength to those who defend the city from attackers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and [he will become] a spirit of justice for the one who sits [i.e., presides] over judgment, // and strength [for] the ones who turn back battle at the city gate.” The Lord will provide internal stability and national security.

verses.zh: 就是这地的人也因酒摇摇晃晃，因浓酒东倒西歪。祭司和先知因浓酒摇摇晃晃，被酒所困，因浓酒东倒西歪。他们错解默示，谬行审判。
verses.en: Even these men[NOTE:1] stagger because of wine;they stumble around because of beer—priests and prophets stagger because of beer,they are confused[NOTE:2] because of wine,they stumble around because of beer;they stagger while seeing prophetic visions,[NOTE:3] they totter while making legal decisions.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “these.” The demonstrative pronoun anticipates “priests and prophets” two lines later.
According to HALOT 135 s.v. III בלע, the verb form is derived from בָּלַע (balaʿ, “confuse”), not the more common בָּלַע (“swallow”). See earlier notes at 3:12 and 9:16.
Heb “in the seeing.”
Heb “[in] giving a decision.”

verses.zh: 因为各席上满了呕吐的污秽，无一处干净。
verses.en: Indeed, all the tablesare covered with vomit,with filth, leaving no clean place.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “filth, without a place.” The Hebrew phrase בְּלִי מָקוֹם (beli maqom, “without a place,” see HALOT 133 s.v. בְּלִי) probably means there is no (clean) space on the table, since it is covered with filth. The translation follows the line division of the MT. Some translations (NASB, ESV, NRSV) move “filth” to the previous line as “filthy vomit,” but the Hebrew lines are no longer balanced.

verses.zh: 讥诮先知的说：他要将知识指教谁呢？要使谁明白传言呢？是那刚断奶离怀的吗？
verses.en: Who is the Lord[NOTE:1] trying to teach?To whom is he explaining a message?[NOTE:2] To those just weaned from milk!To those just taken from their mother’s breast![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “Who is he teaching knowledge? For whom is he explaining a message?” The translation assumes that the Lord is the subject of the verbs “teaching” and “explaining,” and that the prophet is asking the questions. See v. 12. According to some vv. 9-10 record the people’s sarcastic response to the Lord’s message through Isaiah.

Heb “from the breasts.” The words “their mother’s” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The translation assumes that this is the prophet’s answer to the questions asked in the first half of the verse. The Lord is trying to instruct people who are “infants” morally and ethically.

verses.zh: 他竟命上加命，令上加令，律上加律，例上加例，这里一点，那里一点。
verses.en: Indeed, they will hear meaningless gibberish,senseless babbling,a syllable here, a syllable there.[NOTE:1]
notes: The meaning of this verse has been debated. The final line says “a little there, a little there,” while the preceding lines have a series of redundancies (כִּי צַו לָצָו צַו לָצָו קַו לָקָו קַו לָקָו, ki tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav). The present translation assumes that the repetitive syllables are gibberish that resembles baby talk (cf v. 9b) and mimics what the people will hear when foreign invaders conquer the land (v. 11). In this case זְעֵיר (zeʿer, “a little”) refers to the short syllabic structure of the babbling (cf. CEV, REB and see HALOT 1010 s.v. צַו). Some take צַו (tsav) as a derivative of צָוָה (tsavah, “command”) and translate the first part of the statement as “command after command, command after command.” Proponents of this position (followed by many English versions) also take קַו (qav) as a noun meaning “measuring line” (see v. 17), understood here in the abstract sense of “standard” or “rule.”

verses.zh: 先知说：不然，主要藉异邦人的嘴唇和外邦人的舌头对这百姓说话。
verses.en: For with mocking lips and a foreign tonguehe will speak to these people.[NOTE:1]
notes: This verse alludes to the coming Assyrian invasion, when the people will hear a foreign language that sounds like gibberish to them. The Lord is the subject of the verb “will speak,” as v. 12 makes clear. He once spoke in meaningful terms, but in the coming judgment he will speak to them, as it were, through the mouth of foreign oppressors. The apparent gibberish they hear will be an outward reminder that God has decreed their defeat.

verses.zh: 他曾对他们说：你们要使疲乏人得安息，这样才得安息，才得舒畅，他们却不肯听。
verses.en: In the past he said to them,[NOTE:1] “This is where security can be found.Provide security for the one who is exhausted.This is where rest can be found.”[NOTE:2] But they refused to listen.
notes: Heb “who said to them.”
This message encapsulates the Lord’s invitation to his people to find security in his protection and blessing.

verses.zh: 所以，耶和华向他们说的话是命上加命，令上加令，律上加律，例上加例，这里一点，那里一点，以致他们前行仰面跌倒，而且跌碎，并陷入网罗被缠住。
verses.en: So the Lord’s message to them will sound likemeaningless gibberish,senseless babbling,a syllable here, a syllable there.[NOTE:1] As a result, they will fall on their backsides when they try to walk,[NOTE:2] and be injured, ensnared, and captured.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And the message of the Lord will be to them, ‘tsav latsav,’ etc.” See the note at v. 10. In this case the “Lord’s message” is not the foreigner’s strange sounding words (as in v. 10), but the Lord’s repeated appeals to them (like the one quoted in v. 12). As time goes on, the Lord’s appeals through the prophets will have no impact on the people; they will regard prophetic preaching as gibberish.

Heb “as a result they will go and stumble backward.” Perhaps an infant falling as it attempts to learn to walk is the background image here (cf. v. 9b). The Hebrew term לְמַעַן (lemaʿan) could be taken as indicating purpose (“in order that”), rather than simple result. In this case the people’s insensitivity to the message is caused by the Lord as a means of expediting their downfall.
When divine warnings and appeals become gibberish to the spiritually insensitive, they have no guidance and are doomed to destruction.

verses.zh: 所以，你们这些亵慢的人，就是辖管住在耶路撒冷这百姓的，要听耶和华的话。
verses.en: Therefore, listen to the Lord’s message,you who mock,you rulers of these peoplewho reside in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 你们曾说：我们与死亡立约，与阴间结盟；敌军（原文是鞭子）如水涨漫经过的时候，必不临到我们；因我们以谎言为避所，在虚假以下藏身。
verses.en: For you say,“We have made a treaty with death,with Sheol[NOTE:1] we have made an agreement.[NOTE:2] When the overwhelming judgment sweeps by[NOTE:3] it will not reach us.For we have made a lie our refuge,we have hidden ourselves in a deceitful word.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Sheol is the underworld, land of the dead, according to the OT world view.

Elsewhere the noun חֹזֶה (khozeh) refers to a prophet who sees visions. In v. 18 the related term חָזוּת (khazut, “vision”) is used. The parallelism in both verses (note “treaty”) seems to demand a meaning “agreement” for both nouns. Perhaps חֹזֶה and חזוּת are used in a metonymic sense in vv. 15 and 18. Another option is to propose a homonymic root. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:514, and HALOT 301 s.v. II חֹזֶה.
Heb “the overwhelming scourge, when it passes by” (NRSV similar).

“Lie” and “deceitful word” would not be the terms used by the people. They would likely use the words “promise” and “reliable word,” but the prophet substitutes “lie” and “deceitful word” to emphasize that this treaty with death will really prove to be disappointing.

verses.zh: 所以，主耶和华如此说：看哪，我在锡安放一块石头作为根基，是试验过的石头，是稳固根基，宝贵的房角石；信靠的人必不着急。
verses.en: Therefore, this is what the Sovereign Lord, says:“Look, I am laying[NOTE:1] a stone in Zion,an approved[NOTE:2] stone,set in place as a precious cornerstone for the foundation.[NOTE:3] The one who maintains his faith will not panic.[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew text has a third person verb form, which does not agree with the first person suffix that precedes. The form should be emended to יֹסֵד (yosed), a Qal active participle used in a present progressive or imminent future sense.
Traditionally “tested,” but the implication is that it has passed the test and stands approved.

The reality behind the metaphor is not entirely clear from the context. The stone appears to represent someone or something that gives Zion stability. Perhaps the ideal Davidic ruler is in view (see 32:1). Another option is that the image of beginning a building project by laying a precious cornerstone suggests that God is about to transform Zion through judgment and begin a new covenant community that will experience his protection (see 4:3-6; 31:5; 33:20-24; 35:10).
Heb “will not hurry,” i.e., act in panic.

verses.zh: 我必以公平为准绳，以公义为线铊。冰雹必冲去谎言的避所；大水必漫过藏身之处。
verses.en: I will make justice the measuring line,fairness the plumb line;hail will sweep away the unreliable refuge,[NOTE:1] the floodwaters will overwhelm the hiding place.
notes: Heb “[the] refuge, [the] lie.” See v. 15.

verses.zh: 你们与死亡所立的约必然废掉，与阴间所结的盟必立不住。敌军（原文是鞭子）如水涨漫经过的时候，你们必被他践踏；
verses.en: Your treaty with death will be dissolved;[NOTE:1] your agreement[NOTE:2] with Sheol will not last.[NOTE:3] When the overwhelming judgment sweeps by,[NOTE:4] you will be overrun by it.[NOTE:5]
notes: On the meaning of כָּפַר (kafar) in this context, see HALOT 494 s.v. I כפר and J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:515, n. 9.
Normally the noun חָזוּת (khazut) means “vision.” See the note at v. 15.
Or “will not stand” (NIV, NRSV).
See the note at v. 15.
Heb “you will become a trampling place for it.”

verses.zh: 每逢经过必将你们掳去。因为每早晨他必经过，白昼黑夜都必如此。明白传言的必受惊恐。
verses.en: Whenever it sweeps by, it will overtake you;indeed,[NOTE:1] every morning it will sweep by,it will come through during the day and the night.”[NOTE:2] When this announcement is understood,it will cause nothing but terror.
notes: Or “for” (KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV).
The words “it will come through” are supplied in the translation. The verb “will sweep by” does double duty in the parallel structure.

verses.zh: 原来，床榻短，使人不能舒身；被窝窄，使人不能遮体。
verses.en: For the bed is too short to stretch out on,and the blanket is too narrow to wrap around oneself.[NOTE:1]
notes: The bed and blanket probably symbolize their false sense of security. A bed that is too short and a blanket that is too narrow may promise rest and protection from the cold, but in the end they are useless and disappointing. In the same way, their supposed treaty with death will prove useless and disappointing.

verses.zh: 耶和华必兴起，像在毗拉心山；他必发怒，像在基遍谷，好做成他的工，就是非常的工；成就他的事，就是奇异的事。
verses.en: For the Lord will rise up, as he did at Mount Perazim;[NOTE:1] he will rouse himself, as he did in the Valley of Gibeon,[NOTE:2] to accomplish his work,his peculiar work,to perform his task,his strange task.[NOTE:3]
notes: This probably alludes to David’s victory over the Philistines at Baal Perazim. See 2 Sam 5:20.
This probably alludes to the Lord’s victory over the Canaanites at Gibeon, during the days of Joshua. See Josh 10:10-11.
God’s judgment of his own people is called “his peculiar work” and “his strange task,” because he must deal with them the way he treated their enemies in the past.

verses.zh: 现在你们不可亵慢，恐怕捆你们的绑索更结实了；因为我从主―万军之耶和华那里听见，已经决定在全地上施行灭绝的事。
verses.en: So now, do not mock,or your chains will become heavier!For I have heard a message about decreed destruction,from the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies against the entire land.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “the whole earth” (KJV, ASV, NAB, NCV).

verses.zh: 你们当侧耳听我的声音，留心听我的言语。
verses.en: Pay attention and listen to my message.[NOTE:1] Be attentive and listen to what I have to say![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to my voice.”
Heb “to my word”; cf. KJV, ASV, NRSV “hear my speech.”

verses.zh: 那耕地为要撒种的，岂是常常耕地呢？岂是常常开垦耙地呢？
verses.en: Does a farmer just keep on plowing at planting time?[NOTE:1] Does he keep breaking up and harrowing his ground?
notes: Heb “All the day does the plowman plow in order to plant?” The phrase “all the day” here has the sense of “continually, always.” See BDB 400 s.v. יוֹם.

verses.zh: 他拉平了地面，岂不就撒种小茴香，播种大茴香，按行列种小麦，在定处种大麦，在田边种粗麦呢？
verses.en: Once he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter the seed of the caraway plant,sow the seed of the cumin plant,and plant the wheat, barley, and grain in their designated places?[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text reads literally, “place wheat [?], and barley [?], and grain in its territory.” The term שׂוֹרָה (sorah) is sometimes translated “[in] its place,” but the word is unattested in the MT elsewhere. It is probably due to dittography of the immediately following שְׂעֹרָה (seoʿrah, “barley”). The meaning of נִסְמָן (nisman) is also uncertain. It may be due to dittography of the immediately following כֻסֶּמֶת (kussemet, “grain”).

verses.zh: 因为他的　神教导他务农相宜，并且指教他。
verses.en: His God instructs him;he teaches him the principles of agriculture.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he teaches him the proper way; his God instructs him.”

verses.zh: 原来打小茴香，不用尖利的器具，轧大茴香，也不用碌碡（原文是车轮；下同）；但用杖打小茴香，用棍打大茴香。
verses.en: Certainly[NOTE:1] caraway seed is not threshed with a sledge,nor is the wheel of a cart rolled over cumin seed.[NOTE:2] Certainly caraway seed is beaten with a stickand cumin seed with a flail.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “For” (KJV, ASV, NASB).
Both of these seeds are too small to use the ordinary threshing techniques.

A flail was a hand-held threshing tool that had one stick as its handle and another swinging stick attached to its top. The swinging stick was used to beat the grain off of the stalks, which were laying on the ground.

verses.zh: 做饼的粮食是用磨磨碎，因它不必常打；虽用碌碡和马打散，却不磨它。
verses.en: Grain is crushed,though one certainly does not thresh it forever.The wheel of one’s wagon rolls over it,but his horses do not crush it.

verses.zh: 这也是出于万军之耶和华―他的谋略奇妙；他的智慧广大。
verses.en: This also comes from the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,who gives supernatural guidance and imparts great wisdom.[NOTE:1]
notes: Verses 23-29 emphasize that God possesses great wisdom and has established a natural order. Evidence of this can be seen in the way farmers utilize divinely imparted wisdom to grow and harvest crops. God’s dealings with his people will exhibit this same kind of wisdom and order. Judgment will be accomplished according to a divinely ordered timetable and, while severe enough, will not be excessive. Judgment must come, just as planting inevitably follows plowing. God will, as it were, thresh his people, but he will not crush them to the point where they will be of no use to him.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Isaiah 28:1-33:24 forms a literary unit (i.e. six "woe" pronouncements) that deals with Judah's alliance with
Egypt against Assyria in the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah (for the dates of his reign see

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM). I use the dates of these three scholars:
John Bright, 715-687; E. J. Young, 727-699; R. K. Harrison, 716/15-687/86). The historical background
is apparently the time surrounding (i.e. 705-701 B.C.) the invasion of the Assyrian
monarch Sennacherib in 701 B.C.

- Isaiah 28:1-6 deals with the fall of Israel (i.e. the northern tribes after 922 B.C.) to
Assyria. Israel's capital, Samaria, fell in 722 B.C. to Sargon II after a three-year siege.

Verses 7-22 deal with YHWH's judgment of Judah. The covenant people have violated the covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

- Sargon II died in 705 B.C. Many of the vassal nations took this opportunity to rebel
against Assyria. Sennacherib, the next Assyrian monarch, invaded Judah in 701 B.C.
We know from Assyrian documents that he captured forty-six walled villages in Judah and put
down the revolt.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

- Brief Outline of this Chapter

- woe to drunkards of Ephraim, Isa. 28:1-6

- woe to drunk priests and prophets of Judah, Isa. 28:7-13

- woe to the civic leadership of Judah, Isa. 28:14-22

- a parable from agriculture, Isa. 28:23-29

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 28:1-8

1Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim,

And to the fading flower of its glorious beauty,

Which is at the head of the fertile valley

Of those who are overcome with wine!

2Behold, the Lord has a strong and mighty agent;

As a storm of hail, a tempest of destruction,

Like a storm of mighty overflowing waters,

He has cast it down to the earth with His hand.

3The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim is trodden under foot.

4And the fading flower of its glorious beauty,

Which is at the head of the fertile valley,

Will be like the first-ripe fig prior to summer,

Which one sees,

And as soon as it is in his hand,

He swallows it.

5In that day the Lord of hosts will become a beautiful crown

And a glorious diadem to the remnant of His people;

6A spirit of justice for him who sits in judgment,

A strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.

7And these also reel with wine and stagger from strong drink:

The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink,

They are confused by wine, they stagger from strong drink;

They reel while having visions, They totter when rendering judgment.

8For all the tables are full of filthy vomit, without a single clean place.

28:1 "Woe" This term (BDB 222) characterizes this entire section (six "woes," cf. Isa. 28:1; 29:1,15;
30:1; 31:1; 33:1, similar to the six woes of Isa. 5:8-22). The term "woe" characterizes the poetic meter of a
funeral dirge.

▣ "the drunkards of Ephraim" Isaiah 28:1-4 is the prophet's words of judgment to the religious and
political leadership of the Northern Ten Tribes. There is a series of references to their abuse of alcohol
(cf. Isa. 28:1 (twice), 3,7; Hosea 7:5). Alcohol abuse is often used as imagery of poor judgments which
result in divine judgment. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WINE AND STRONG DRINK.

28:2 "the Lord has a strong and mighty agent" This refers to the Assyrian empire sent by YHWH
(cf. Isa. 8:7; 10:5-6) to punish Israel. The destruction of the Northern Ten Tribes was consummated
in the fall of the capital city Samaria after a three year siege by Sargon II in
722 B.C. (cf. 2 Kgs. 17:6; 18:9-12). All her people were exiled to Media.
The vast majority never returned.

Notice how the Lord's agent is characterized.

- strong

- mighty

- a storm of hail (cf. Isa. 30:30)

- a tempest of destruction

- a storm of mighty overflowing waters (cf. Isa. 8:7-8)

is captured and occupied by foreigners.

28:16 This verse is a shocking change of mode, a theological reversal of hope amidst judgment. YHWH's
redemptive universal plan reveals itself again. Messiah will come! It is only one verse, but what a verse!

This is a series of Messianic titles using "construction" imagery.

- The term "stone" (BDB 6) is often used of God; however, the term "cornerstone" (BDB 819) has a
unique connection with the Messiah (cf. Ps. 118:22; Matt. 21:42, 44: Luke 20:17; Acts 4:11;
Rom. 9:33; 10:11; Eph. 2:20; 1 Pet. 2:6-8).

- The term "tested" (BDB 103) is an Egyptian loan word for a fine grain stone suitable for carving.
This seems to mean that God is going to inscribe the cornerstone with the phrase found in 16d. The
key to this thought is the term "believes" (cf. Isa. 30:15 for a similar emphasis on "trust").

- The term "foundation" (BDB 414) is found only here and 2 Chr. 8:16, where it refers to Solomon's
laying the foundation of the temple. Notice that this foundation is "firmly placed"
(NASB margin, "well-laid"). The Hebrew has another doubling of a word. This is where the
translation "firmly" or "well-laid" comes from.
